items.title: Solving for Final Velocity and Angle

source_refs.note: Solving for Final Velocity and Angle: a main subheading of 2.11 Inelastic collision in two dimensions, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 46-46.

blocks.text: The magnitude of the final velocity v⃗f can be found by squaring and then adding equations (2.39) and (2.40).

blocks.text_alt: vf = √([(m₁v₁i cos θ₁ + m₂v₂i cos θ₂)/M]² + [(m₁v₁i sin θ₁ + m₂v₂i sin θ₂)/M]²)   (2.41)

blocks.text: The angle φ of the final velocity v⃗f relative to the x-axis is obtained by dividing the equations (2.40) by (2.41):

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The angle φ comes from dividing Eq. (2.40) by Eq. (2.39) (the y-momentum equation by the x-momentum equation), not by (2.41).

blocks.text_alt: φ = tan⁻¹[(m₁v₁i sin θ₁ + m₂v₂i sin θ₂)/(m₁v₁i cos θ₁ + m₂v₂i cos θ₂)]   (2.42)

blocks.text: Here φ is the direction of common velocity of two bodies with x-axis which stick together after inelastic collision. Substituting the value of m₁, m₂, M, θ₁, θ₂, φ and v⃗₁i, v⃗₂i, v⃗f in equations (2.39) and (2.40), the law of conservation of momentum in above case can be proved.
